reviews.one_line_contribution: On ALFWorld, rewrite the object-placement rule at three binding scopes (one receptacle per class globally, per (scene,class), per game) and show that the scope fixes the smallest cached static prefix that matches top-k retrieval — a sentence, a table, or nothing but the instance's own planted duplicate — thereby splitting a measured retrieval gain into a compilable part and a near-duplicate-leakage part.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Closest verified methodological threat: ExecRetrieval (arXiv:2609.01865, verified via hf) plants controlled, execution-verified near-clone variants of each query's canonical solution into the retrieval pool to measure whether retrieval discriminates correct from near-duplicate-but-wrong items. That is the same 'plant a controlled duplicate and read off the effect' move, but on code retrieval, scored on ranking rather than task success, with no compiled-static arm and no scope manipulation, so it does not make this proposal's claim. For the P6(b) branch specifically, The Compliance Trap (arXiv:2607.10608, verified via s2, E-P-R trajectory-level framework for how agents consume conflicting retrieved memory) already shows early adoption of conflicting memory and weak recovery; P6(b) is a narrower special case (does a correct rank-1 self-duplicate survive two contradicting neighbours), so that branch is an increment rather than a new finding. EvoMemBench (arXiv:2605.18421, verified via s2) uses 'memory scope' for in-episode vs cross-episode and reports long-context beating memory methods — adjacent to the whole-bank arm, a different axis; the proposal is right that it does not manipulate binding scope or duplicate rate. AgentCL (arXiv:2606.02461, verified via s2) supplies controlled task streams and transfer-gain metrics but no compiled-prompt arm. SWE-ContextBench (arXiv:2602.08316, verified via s2, 10 cit) shows retrieved prior experience helps most on hard tasks but draws relatedness from dependency links rather than manipulating it. No verified paper makes the central claim.
reviews.strongest_objection: The headline is largely constructed rather than discovered, and the automated entailment check reaches the same conclusion for P6(a). Instance-scope relocation is defined so that game A's receptacle is uninformative about game B's; 'no spillover' (N(0.5) = residual(0)) is therefore what the construction guarantees, and the only escape route — generic search-strategy transfer from seeing other instances' trajectories — is never isolated by an arm. Worse, the added foreign duplicates can only displace same-scene train items at ranks 1-3, pushing N(0.5) down, so the prediction is protected from both sides. The same objection applies to the ladder's spine: at global scope the compiled sentence is by construction an information-complete statement of the relocation rule, and at instance scope the proposal declares that no sub-linear prefix exists rather than testing it ('the O(instances) duplicate-row table ... is not run'). What remains genuinely empirical is only whether Qwen3-32B can execute a stated rule, look up a row, or copy a 25-step expert plan — a prompt-format and lookup-ability result, not a result about memory. Second, the title promises an audit of how much of a memory gain is leakage, but no published benchmark's duplicate rate is measured anywhere in the design; s is hand-set to {0, 0.5, 1} and the slope over s is explicitly demoted to descriptive, so the paper cannot say what fraction of any real reported memory gain is leakage. Third, P5's +28 threshold is anchored to nothing measured: static3-relocated's level under the 25-step relocated regime is unknown, and with the node's observed ~0.87 ceiling a strong static arm could force falsification for headroom reasons rather than for the claim. Fourth, P7 confounds 'the whole bank cannot replace the query' with prefix length and serial position — an ~11k-token 80-item prefix versus a ~430-token one — and blind1's -3 net length bound was measured at 430 tokens, so it does not cover this regime.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Demote P6(a) and promote P0 and P4 to the headline: 'Measurement C's +17.2 net retrieval residual compiles into ~20 class-location sentences (or a 274-row table)' is the result that is neither entailed nor already known, and it needs no relocation machinery. (2) Make the no-spillover claim earn its keep with the bank-composition control the entailment check names: hold bank size and rank-1-3 composition fixed and vary only whether the extra same-scene items are other games' exact duplicates or matched non-duplicate trajectories, with s at 0.25 and 0.75, so the strategy-transfer channel is shown to exist before its absence is claimed. (3) Run the instance-scope row table (one (game -> receptacle) row per eval game, ~274 rows, the same size as the scene-scope table already budgeted) as a confirmatory cell rather than declaring it out of scope; it is one cell and it is the only arm that can refute 'instance scope requires a query'. (4) Anchor P5 to the measured static3-relocated level in the same cell and state the achievable ceiling under the 25-step budget, or restate P5 as a fraction of headroom. (5) Add a position/length control to P7: the same 80-item prefix with the duplicate at rank 1, middle and last, plus an 80-item prefix with the duplicate removed, so 'no query' is separated from lost-in-the-middle (cf. 2605.27105, 2505.15561). (6) Measure the actual (goal, scene, init) duplicate rate of at least one published agent-memory benchmark stream and place it on the s axis, so the leakage index refers to something outside this design.
reviews.missing_baseline: The instance-scope compiled row table — one (game -> target receptacle) row per eval game as a single cached static prefix, at most 274 rows, i.e. exactly the size of the scene-scope table the plan already runs. The proposal explicitly declines it ('the O(instances) duplicate-row table is the whole-bank arm in row form and is not run'), but it is the direct test of the ladder's punchline that instance scope admits no static substitute, and it is the arm most likely to break it: if a reader can find its own game's row among 274 rows as easily as its scene's row among 274 rows, then everything compiles and the ladder collapses into 'retrieval is never necessary here'. Omitting an arm that costs one cell and is the sole falsifier of the top-level claim will read to a reviewer as protecting the result. Secondary omission: a content-matched non-duplicate bank-composition control at instance scope (fix bank size and rank composition, swap other games' exact duplicates for matched non-duplicate trajectories), without which P6(a) has no arm that could produce its falsifier.
reviews.preprint_collision: No verified collision. (3) closest named method: 'ExpeL agent experience learning ALFWorld retrieved trajectories versus compiled rules static prompt' -> [hf] 2308.10144 ExpeL, 2605.16986 Skills on the Fly, 2601.22758 AutoRefine, 2505.00234 self-generated in-context examples, 2410.07484 / 2504.15785 WALL-E rule learning, 2010.03768 ALFWorld — several compile rules from trajectories, none reports the compiled artifact as a token-matched substitute for retrieval under a scope manipulation. (5) --recent: 'fraction of agent memory improvement attributable to task overlap dose response duplicate task stream ablation' -> [hf] 2608.07169, 2608.06811, 2607.10608, 2607.08716, 2606.14571, 2602.02196 TIDE, 2601.11653 — empty on the specific claim. IDs I verified: 2511.20857 Evo-Memory (s2, 123 cit), 2512.10696 ReMe (s2, ACL, 55 cit), 2605.18421 EvoMemBench (s2, 7 cit, two axes memory scope/content as the proposal describes), 2606.02461 AgentCL (s2, 1 cit, controlled task streams + MemProbe as described), 2602.08316 SWE-ContextBench (s2, 10 cit), 2607.10608 Compliance Trap (s2, E-P-R framework as described), 2107.06499 (s2, ACL, 971 cit), 2411.03923 ConTAM (hf), 2609.01865 ExecRetrieval (hf). Not verified: 2311.04850 (rephrased-sample contamination) and the brief-level ids the novelty argument does not rest on. One caveat the proposal's check misses: it ran no query in the compiled/distilled-skills literature its own brief names (ICAL 2406.14596, SkillEvolBench 2605.24117, MemAPO 2603.21520, CLEAR 2604.07487) even though P2 and P4 are compiled-vs-retrieved claims, and none in the RAG position / long-context literature that governs P7's interpretation (2505.15561, 2605.27105). Those two gaps are where a scoop is most likely sitting, and an empty search I did not run is reported here as not run, not as novelty.

reviews.one_line_contribution: A controlled ALFWorld manipulation of how widely a planted object-receptacle binding holds (one receptacle per class everywhere / per (scene,class) / per game) that reads off, at each scope, the smallest static cached prompt that matches top-k retrieval, and how much of the retrieval gain at instance scope is nothing but the eval game's own duplicate trajectory.
reviews.closest_prior_work: No single verified paper makes this claim. The two closest, both verified via the literature command (s2cli.py paper): (1) EvoMemBench, arXiv:2605.18421 (verified, S2: 'two axes: memory scope (in-episode vs. cross-episode) and memory content'; long-context baselines outperform specialized memory methods). It does not threaten the binding-scope manipulation — its 'scope' is temporal, not the scope over which a binding holds — but its headline that long context beats memory methods pre-empts a good part of the whole-bank message the proposal builds arms for (P7's interest is then 'why does the whole bank lose here', not 'does it lose'). (2) The Compliance Trap, arXiv:2607.10608 (verified, S2: Enter-Propagation-Recovery, agents adopt conflicting retrieved memory early and compound errors). It is cited, but it substantially pre-empts P6(b): if agents already fail to discount contradicted memory, 'conflict ≈ neutral' is the expected direction, and the proposal frames it as a discovery rather than a replication under a cleaner manipulation. One item my search turned up that the proposal does NOT cite and should: ExecRetrieval, arXiv:2609.01865 (hf, 2026-09-01), which plants controlled, execution-verified single-edit near-clone variants of each query's canonical item in the retrieval pool — the same planted-near-duplicate design move, in code retrieval, judged on embedding discrimination rather than on downstream gain share. Also adjacent and uncited: 'Right Family, Wrong Skill', arXiv:2606.10388 (hf), on same-family sibling exposure in skill retrieval, which is close to the conflict-neighbour arm.
reviews.strongest_objection: Most rungs of the ladder are true by construction, so the ladder measures Qwen3-32B's reading competence rather than a property of memory. The relocation rules define the information content of the bank: at global scope the 20-sentence compiled prefix is an information-complete restatement of the planted rule, at scene scope the (scene,class) table is likewise complete, and at instance scope 'no static prefix smaller than one row per instance exists' is a definition the proposal states outright ('the instance-scope static substitute is defined as a prefix whose size does not grow with the number of instances; the O(instances) duplicate-row table ... is not run'). P2 and P4 can therefore only be falsified by a format/lookup failure, and the headline P6(a) is worse: the automated entailment check calls it near-entailed and it is — instance-scope relocation is built so another game's duplicate carries zero information about this game's placement, and the added foreign duplicates can only displace same-scene train items at ranks 1-3, pushing N(0.5) down, i.e. toward confirmation. The design contains no positive control showing that a strategy-transfer channel is detectable at all on this node, so P6(a) is a null the construction guarantees, reported as a finding. Strip the entailed rungs and what is left that could genuinely surprise is P0 (does the natural bank's +17.2 compile into a ~430-token class-location table?) and P6(b) — one confirmatory cell and one manipulated pair out of 22, for ~13.5k episodes. A secondary version of the same objection: P7's 'whole bank loses ≥14 net' is confounded by prefix length and item set, so a confirmation is readable as a many-shot dilution result (cf. arXiv:2510.16809, arXiv:2411.05000 in the brief), not as evidence that the query is doing work.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Re-centre the paper on the cells that are not construction-determined and cut the ones that are. (1) Promote P0 to the headline: run the natural-bank scope estimate properly — class-location table, (scene,class) table, and a scrambled-binding version of each, paired with k3 and static3 on Measurement C's games and seeds — and report where the natural ALFWorld bank actually sits on the scope axis. That is a result about a benchmark the field uses, and it is not entailed. (2) Before claiming 'no spillover', run the bank-composition control the entailment check names: hold bank size, item count and rank composition fixed at instance scope and vary only whether the extra same-scene items are other games' exact duplicates or matched non-duplicate trajectories, plus a dose at s=0.25/0.75; show the strategy-transfer channel can be detected before reporting its absence. (3) Anchor P5's +28 to the measured absolute success of static3-relocated under the 25-step relocated regime and report the headroom; as written the threshold can fail for ceiling reasons rather than because the reader ignores its own duplicate. (4) Give P7 a length-matched control (80 same-scene items with the duplicate deleted, and 80 other-scene items) so a confirmation cannot be read as context dilution. (5) Either run the WebShop scope-statistic prediction or drop the framing that the scope of bindings is a general predictor — one environment, one reader, one synthetic relocation family cannot support it.
reviews.missing_baseline: A scrambled-binding placebo for every compiled static arm: the same sentence list / (scene,class) table with the class-to-receptacle mapping permuted, byte-identical in format and token count. Without it, 'the compiled sentence matches retrieval' cannot distinguish a reader that consumed the stated binding from a reader that ignored the prefix and found the object by search inside 25 steps — exactly the ambiguity blind1 was introduced to resolve for exemplars in Measurement C, and it is not carried over to the compiled arms. Two smaller omissions a reviewer would also ask for: a k=0 relocated arm per scope (the absolute anchor for how much room the bindings have, ~548 episodes each), and the instance-scope bank-composition control (matched non-duplicate same-scene items at fixed bank size) without which P6(a)'s null has no positive control.
reviews.preprint_collision: No verified collision. My searches (all answered by the literature command, s2cli.py, with both channels reporting ok — s2=ok hf=ok on every call; WebSearch is unavailable in this session and was not used): (a) mechanism, --recent: 'binding scope near-duplicate leakage experience bank agent memory gain' -> 14 hits, closest arXiv:2607.10608 (Compliance Trap), arXiv:2605.11325 (Tenure, typed schemas with 'scope isolation' — storage scope, not binding scope), arXiv:2606.15903, arXiv:2512.16962; none manipulates duplicate rate or binding scope. (b) mechanism, all years: 'controlled duplicate rate in experience bank retrieval gain compiled static prompt agent' -> 16 hits, closest arXiv:2606.10388 (Right Family, Wrong Skill), arXiv:2608.11079 (SkillZip), arXiv:2602.08316 (SWE-ContextBench); no compiled-prompt-vs-retrieval arm at matched tokens with a manipulated duplicate rate. (c) closest named method: 'EvoMemBench memory scope in-episode cross-episode long-context baseline agent memory benchmark' --> arXiv:2605.18421 confirmed plus arXiv:2606.05684, arXiv:2605.12493, arXiv:2602.16313, arXiv:2606.13681; none compiles a bank into a static prefix or reports gain as a function of duplicate rate. (d) home literature: 'planted near-duplicate demonstration retrieval versus fixed exemplars in-context example selection inflation' -> only generic ICL selection work (arXiv:2405.00200, arXiv:2605.13511, arXiv:2309.07900), consistent with the proposal's claim that the contamination/dedup literature has not been applied to experience banks. (e) 'how much of agent memory benchmark gain comes from repeated near identical tasks leakage audit' --recent -> benchmark-validity work (arXiv:2605.12673 BenchJack, arXiv:2607.02577) but no leakage-share audit of memory gains. (f) 'ALFWorld object receptacle location instance specific binding memory retrieval scene' -> nothing on planted bindings. ID verification: I verified 2605.18421, 2606.02461, 2607.10608, 2511.20857, 2512.10696, 2602.08316, 2607.26497 and 2603.04814 with s2cli.py paper; all resolve and match the proposal's characterisations, including the important one that EvoMemBench's 'scope' is in-episode vs cross-episode and not binding scope. I did not verify 2604.07791, 2605.13880, 2603.21520, 2604.07487, 2605.24117 or the ConTAM/dedup IDs, which the proposal's argument leans on less directly. Judging the proposal's own check: it is better than most in this round — four query classes including a home-literature query without agent/memory vocabulary, both channels named, two IDs verified, and an honest statement of what each near-miss does and does not do. Its gap is recency at the very edge: it misses arXiv:2609.01865 (ExecRetrieval, 2026-09-01), which plants controlled near-clone variants of each query's canonical item in a retrieval pool, and arXiv:2606.10388; neither collides with the central claim, but both are the kind of preprint a reviewer will produce, and the second is a direct precedent for the conflict-neighbour construction. Novelty is scored on what I verified: the binding-scope manipulation against compiled static arms is unclaimed in the literature I could reach, so no cap applies.

reviews.one_line_contribution: On a synthetically relocated ALFWorld it manipulates the scope at which object-receptacle bindings hold (one rule per class, per (scene,class), or per game) and the rate at which an eval game's own expert trajectory is planted in the bank, then asks at each scope whether a rule-written static prefix (a sentence, a table, or nothing) matches top-k retrieval and how much of the retrieval residual over the best static arm is replay of the game's own near-duplicate.
reviews.closest_prior_work: EvoMemBench (arXiv:2605.18421, verified via s2cli paper, S2 channel, 2026-05-18, 7 citations): it organizes agent memory along a memory-scope axis (in-episode vs cross-episode) crossed with content, and reports that long-context baselines still outperform specialized memory methods. That is the same headline shape as the whole-bank arm here, and it pre-empts the 'does a query buy anything over the bank in context' half of the contribution; it does not manipulate binding scope, does not vary duplicate rate, and has no compiled static arm, so it does not scoop the ladder itself. Two other verified threats: The Compliance Trap (arXiv:2607.10608, verified, S2) already gives a trajectory-level account of agents adopting conflicting retrieved memory with compounding errors and weak recovery - P6(b) is close to a single-cell replication of that mechanism on ALFWorld with the correct duplicate pinned at rank 1, and the proposal predicts the null direction without engaging the prior evidence that points the other way. ExecRetrieval (arXiv:2609.01865, verified, S2, 2026-09-01) is the closest methodological neighbour to the planting design: it plants execution-verified single-edit near-clone distractors of each query's canonical item in the retrieval pool to measure whether embeddings discriminate correct from near-clone-but-wrong - the same 'construct the pool so the near-duplicate is controlled' move, in code retrieval rather than agent memory and scored on retrieval, not task success. Finally, the conceptual claim 'near-duplicate overlap inflates a measured gain' is owned by the dedup/contamination literature the proposal itself cites (2107.06499 verified, HF); transposing it to experience banks is a real but incremental step.
reviews.strongest_objection: The ladder's results are largely fixed by the construction, not measured. The scope taxonomy is the experimenter's own relocation rule, so 'the smallest static substitute grows with binding scope' is an information-theoretic consequence of how the three worlds were built: under a global relocation rule one sentence is a sufficient statistic of the bank; under a scene rule the (scene,class) table is; under a per-game rule nothing short of per-instance rows is. What remains empirical is only the narrow reader-consumption question of whether Qwen3-32B applies a stated rule as well as it applies a shown trajectory (P2, P4) and whether it replays its own expert trajectory (P5, which is a positive control dressed as a prediction). The headline is weaker still: at instance scope another game's duplicate carries zero information about this game by construction, so P6(a)'s no-spillover is near-entailed (the automated check agrees), and its only falsifying channel - generic search-strategy transfer - is never isolated by a bank-composition control; worse, adding foreign duplicates can only displace informative same-scene train items at ranks 1-3, which pushes N(0.5) down and thus away from the falsifier. And the title's quantity - how much of a memory gain is near-duplicate leakage - is never measured on any bank that was not built to contain the answer: natural ALFWorld is class-scope with no instance duplicates, gets exactly one anchor cell (P0), and every leakage number in the paper comes from duplicates the experimenter planted at a rate the experimenter chose. A second, sharper technical objection: the +14 and +28 margins are absolute net points inherited from the natural bank (k0 = 0.54, k3 = 0.81-0.87), but relocation plus a 25-step budget changes the base rate and the headroom in each scope, and no per-scope normalization or base-rate check is specified, so P5 can be falsified for ceiling reasons and the three rungs of the ladder are not on comparable scales.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Run the instance-scope row table you declined: a cached static prefix of one binding row per eval game (<= 274 rows, ~3k tokens, the same size as the scene-scope table you do run) plus a per-game one-line binding prefix. That turns 'no static substitute exists at instance scope' from a definition into a measurement, and it separates 'the duplicate's value is one bit of binding information' from 'the duplicate's value is trajectory replay' - the actual scientific question at that rung. If the reader finds its own row among 274, P7 and the headline collapse, which is exactly what a confirmatory design should risk. (2) Add the bank-composition control the entailment check names: hold bank size and rank-1/2/3 composition fixed and swap other games' exact duplicates for matched non-duplicate same-scene trajectories, with a dose at s = 0.25/0.75, so the strategy-transfer channel is shown to exist before its absence is claimed. (3) Re-anchor margins per scope: measure k0 and static3-relocated in each relocated world first, pre-register margins as fractions of that scope's own headroom, and report the ceiling. (4) Put one leakage number on an unmanipulated bank - delete (goal text, scene) near-duplicates from the natural train bank and re-run k3 - so the title's claim touches a bank nobody constructed for it. (5) State a family-wise plan: eight pre-registered predictions over 22-25 cells at two seeds, several of them equivalence tests at margin 8 with ~5-net half-widths, needs a multiplicity policy. (6) Cite and engage arXiv:2604.27003 (When Continual Learning Moves to Memory), which my search returned and the related work misses.
reviews.missing_baseline: The instance-scope binding-row arm - a cached per-game one-line static prefix naming the game's own class-receptacle binding, and its query-free counterpart, the <= 274-row instance table. The proposal defines this away ('the instance-scope static substitute is a prefix whose size does not grow with the number of instances; the O(instances) duplicate-row table is the whole-bank arm in row form and is not run'), but the row table is ~3k tokens and fits context, unlike the 80-trajectory whole-bank arm at ~11k, and it is the same artifact class as the <= 274-row table that IS run at scene scope; the asymmetry is what makes P7 look confirmed. Second omission: a rank-1 content control at instance scope (duplicate replaced by a matched non-duplicate same-class, same-scene trajectory at fixed bank size and token count), without which the s-manipulation confounds 'the duplicate' with 'bank composition at ranks 1-3'. Third, minor: a random-3 same-scene retrieval placebo at instance scope; blind1's -3 net bounds a wrong-type length effect on the natural bank, not a same-scene random draw in the relocated world.
reviews.preprint_collision: No verified collision. I could not check 2411.03923 or 2311.04850 (home-literature citations, not load-bearing for novelty) - unverified. My own searches, all answered by channel (a); channel (b) WebSearch is unavailable in this session and was not used: (Q1, --recent) 'near-duplicate leakage agent experience memory retrieval gain duplicate rate' -> 12 hits, nearest 2607.10608, 2606.02461, 2606.24595, and one item the proposal does not cite, 2604.27003 (When Continual Learning Moves to Memory: experience reuse in LLM agents, memory design trades transfer against forgetting); none manipulates duplicate rate. (Q2) 'compiled static prompt matches retrieval agent experience memory ALFWorld exemplars' -> 2605.16986 Skills on the Fly, 2605.05413 From History to State, 2605.20616 Auto-Dreamer, 2606.06087 LatentSkill, 2505.00234 self-generated in-context examples; none reports retrieval minus a compiled static arm as a function of binding scope. (Q3, closest named method) 'EvoMemBench memory scope benchmark long-context baseline outperforms memory methods' -> 2605.18421 (verified), plus 2606.13681 EvoArena; confirms the scope framing exists but at a different axis. (Q4, --recent) 'controlled duplicate rate planted identical task trajectory bank measures how much memory gain is leakage' -> effectively empty on the mechanism (Omega-S, HiMPO, 2606.10229 demonstration-curation metrics); reported as empty, not as evidence. (Q5) 'object receptacle location binding household embodied agent memory generalizes across scenes instance specific' -> MEMENTO 2505.16348 (verified, S2, 12 cits: episodic memory gives personalized knowledge plus in-context learning benefit in embodied personalization) and KARMA 2409.14908, CAPEAM 2308.07241; none manipulates binding scope. Weaknesses of the proposal's check that I would flag: it runs no query in the pool-construction vocabulary that would surface ExecRetrieval 2609.01865 (verified, 2026-09-01, planted execution-verified near-clone distractors per query - the same methodological move, in code retrieval), and none in the embodied/household-memory vocabulary where instance bindings actually live (MEMENTO); its negatives are abstract-level only, which is worth stating explicitly rather than as 'no collision found'.
